task: Reconstruct N58 three-gain kinetic regularization and test quantitative, Landau, and hydrodynamic bridges.
scientific_status: source_derived_unreviewed; local rank proof reconstructed; fixture diagnostic replayed; no external validation or priority claim

claims.statement: For every fixed nonaxial endpoint, positive scale/sign triple, and real-analytic axial profile triple in the source interface, Phi_3(t1,t2,t3,L1,L2,L3)=(t3,x3,v3) has rank 7 almost everywhere on (0,infinity)^3 x R^9, including the strictly ordered history region.
assumptions: v0 has nonzero component perpendicular to e3
Each cold profile is axial and real analytic on positive times
Collision increments obey k_i=n_i cross L_i
The three scales and signs are fixed and positive
claims.information_and_cost: Three gain steps; 3 time parameters and 9 redundant plane coordinates (12 total); the finite-temperature pullback uses 9 spectator coordinates (21 total).
claims.proof_status: reconstructed from the immutable three_gain_regularization.txt and THREE_GAIN_RANK_CHECK.md; exact rational fixture program replayed with 24/24 checks passing
claims.falsifier: A profile/endpoint in this interface for which a rank-7 minor is identically zero on the connected domain; the profile-independent witness rules this out.
evidence: OA363 source labels nc:plane-parameters, nc:uniform-pullback, lem:five-gain-rank

claims.statement: Two gains cannot give rank 7 in this redundant plane parameterization.
assumptions: Each gain uses one time and one L in R^3
The L component parallel to its current normal is a gauge direction
claims.conclusion: Two gains have at most 8 parameters and at least two independent gauge kernel directions, hence rank at most 6.
claims.comparator: The pinned OA363 source uses five gains; N58 reduces to the minimum three for this seven-coordinate submersion task.

claims.statement: For convergent endpoints with a nonaxial limiting velocity, V_n^3 f_n at the endpoint tends to zero when 0<=f_n<=2 and f_n tends to zero in measure on compact subsets away from the velocity axis, provided the unchanged source kernel, tail, endpoint, axis, compactness, and finite-temperature C1-convergence lemmas hold.
claims.status: conditional; R package downstream audit supplies the three-gain substitutions, while upstream lemmas remain imported
claims.quantifiers: Fixed a>0 and compact parameter truncations first; then n tends to infinity; deleted-tail, axis, scale, endpoint-time, and time-gap errors are sent to zero in source order.
claims.falsifier: A retained positive-mass sequence violating the stated pullback conclusion while satisfying all source kernel and C1 hypotheses.
evidence: R downstream audit d-2dac2410284ca0a7, asset SHA256 581d3c24b6bff3c5fd77a187a5ed59befbd2fc5a0370663ed0153f5031a928dd

claims.statement: On a parameter chart U x Z where each u-map Phi_n(.,z) is at most N-to-one and |det D_u Phi_n|>=sigma>0, bounded parameter density |a_n|<=A gives integral |F_n(Phi_n)a_n| <= A N |Z| sigma^(-1) ||F_n||_1.
assumptions: U subset R^7 and Z are bounded measurable parameter sets
The seven-coordinate Jacobian minor is uniformly bounded below by sigma
The map multiplicity is uniformly at most N
The input has an explicit L1 norm or measure-of-superlevel-set modulus
claims.proof_status: proved here by area formula and Fubini
claims.scope: Applies locally near the explicit N58 witness after selecting coordinates and shrinking the chart; does not bound the whole gain integral without a quantified critical-set remainder and a finite uniform chart cover.

claims.statement: Almost-everywhere rank, uniformly bounded densities, bounded F_n, and convergence of F_n to zero in measure imply only qualitative pullback convergence; they imply no universal quantitative rate.
claims.counterexample: Phi(u,z)=u on (0,1)^7 x (0,1)^q and F_n=1_(0,r_n)x(0,1)^6 for any arbitrarily slowly decreasing r_n. Then rank is 7 everywhere, F_n tends to zero in measure, but the pullback integral is r_n times the z-volume.
claims.status: proved counterexample to a rate claim under N58 assumptions
missing_inputs_for_rate: An explicit L1 or superlevel-set decay modulus for F_n
A quantitative lower-singular-value sublevel estimate for D Phi_3
Uniform chart and density constants over all retained collision parameters

claims.statement: Under a grazing angular support theta<=delta and a nondegenerate Landau normalization int sin^2(theta)b_delta >= c, the N58-style positive hot generator A_delta=2P_delta(B,h)-nu_delta,B h has mass at least c(B,h) delta^(-2) for fixed nonzero compactly supported separated B,h with positive continuous kinetic factor.
claims.proof: beta_delta=int b_delta >= c delta^(-2); elastic gain symmetry gives int A_delta = beta_delta int int |v-w|^gamma B(w)h(v) dw dv, whose pair integral is bounded below on the separated compact supports.
claims.status: derived obstruction to this positive-branching transfer only
claims.counterexample_boundary: The full signed linearization includes -nu_delta,h B and retains the cancellation. This does not imply Landau uniqueness or rule out a different signed construction.

claims.statement: N58 rank alone gives no Landau entropy-dissipation or coercivity lower bound.
claims.reason: The rank map contains no density-gradient information or lower bound on the Landau diffusion quadratic form. The complete signed operator estimate needed for the proposed amplification route is absent. Independent Landau coercivity results exist under separate hypotheses and are not implied by this rank map.
claims.exact_missing_lemma: A uniform lower bound for the complete signed Landau linearization on a specified off-axis observable, while the total density remains nonnegative and has controlled entropy production; alternatively, for ordinary coercivity, a stated function class and quantitative entropy-dissipation estimate with explicit mass/energy/entropy constants.
known-independent-prior-art: L. Desvillettes (2015), Coulomb Landau entropy dissipation bounded below by a weighted H^1 norm of sqrt(f); see literature list.

claims.statement: N58 rank/nonconcentration does not yield a kinetic-to-fluid or particle-to-fluid hydrodynamic limit.
missing_inputs: A specified Knudsen/Boltzmann-Grad scaling and sequence of solutions or particle systems
Uniform entropy, energy, moment, and local-conservation control
Compactness and identification of limiting moments and constitutive coefficients
For particle fluctuations, horizon/data/graph-size-uniform recollision and centering moduli

literature.citation: L. Desvillettes, On asymptotics of the Boltzmann equation when the collisions become grazing, Transport Theory and Statistical Physics 21 (1992), 259-276.
literature.comparison: Rigorous grazing asymptotics in a linearized setting; not a consequence of three hard-sphere gains.

literature.citation: R. Alexandre and C. Villani, On the Landau approximation in plasma physics, Ann. Inst. H. Poincare Anal. Non Lineaire 21 (2004), 61-95.
literature.comparison: Spatially dependent grazing approximation under finite mass, energy, entropy and entropy-production bounds; finite-time scope.

literature.citation: J. Carrillo, M. Delgadino and J. Wu, Boltzmann to Landau from the Gradient Flow Perspective, arXiv:2107.07252, v2 2022.
literature.comparison: Frames the grazing bridge through lower-semicontinuous convergence of entropy dissipation.

literature.citation: L. Desvillettes, Entropy dissipation estimates for the Landau equation in the Coulomb case and applications, Journal of Functional Analysis 269 (2015), 1359-1403.
literature.comparison: An independent Coulomb Landau entropy-dissipation lower bound by a weighted H^1 norm of sqrt(f), with homogeneous-equation consequences; it uses Landau structure and does not follow from the N58 collision-map rank.

literature.citation: C. Bardos, F. Golse and C. D. Levermore, Fluid dynamic limits of kinetic equations II: Convergence proofs for the Boltzmann equation, Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 46 (1993), 667-753.
literature.comparison: Uses relative entropy and appropriately scaled renormalized solutions, with conservation and compactness information.

literature.citation: F. Golse and L. Saint-Raymond, The Navier-Stokes limit of the Boltzmann equation for bounded collision kernels, Invent. Math. 155 (2004), 81-161.
literature.comparison: A rigorous scaled-equation hydrodynamic limit; the gain-rank map supplies none of its scaling or entropy framework.

literature.citation: T. Bodineau, I. Gallagher, L. Saint-Raymond and S. Simonella, Dynamics of dilute gases at equilibrium: from the atomistic description to fluctuating hydrodynamics, arXiv:2210.11812.
literature.comparison: Particle-level equilibrium fluctuating hydrodynamics uses covariance asymptotics and a Wick rule.
